correctness.rationale: The log MGF equals V_p t² M_p(t)/2 and the scale variational identity is c*(p)=sup_{t>=0}(1-M_p(t)^{-1})/t. Its t=0 value m_p=(1+124p)/(3(1+24p)); Taylor differentiation yields Phi_p'(0)=-(16576p²-952p+1)/(36(1+24p)²)<0 uniformly over p<=10^-4. At p=0 a coefficientwise strict comparison M_0(t)<1/(1-t/3) for 0<t<3 plus Phi<1/t for t>=3 proves global endpoint dominance. At p=10^-4, exact finite positive Taylor lower bounds e²>7 and e^10>22000 imply M_p(2)>1/(1-2m_p) and Phi_p(2)>m_p. Uniform local-slope negativity, joint continuity on compact [0,10^-4]x[0,3], and infimum of positive global-gap parameters yield p*>0 where zero and a bounded-away-from-zero interior argument both attain the maximum. The proof asserts neither uniqueness nor an exact p*.
